name: Spokane River (Spokane – Plese Flats)
blurb: City-to-state-park run under the bluffs of Riverside State Park, with Bowl and Pitcher's basalt rapids.

sections.notes: Mostly Class II with two Class III rapids (AW). Spring runoff flows are big and dangerous. AW lists the reach as 6.8 mi; access mileages give ~6.5. Discover Pass required at Riverside State Park (Plese Flats).
sections.routeReview: Approximate river-course overview only. The line follows the Spokane River corridor through whitewater; it does not identify runnable chutes, scouting trails, portages or exact landing connections.

notices.title: Seasonal access and wildfire restrictions
notices.text: Plese Flats is marked open on the October 28, 2026 park recovery map, but its season ends at the first snow. Nearby trails and fire-damaged areas remain closed. Confirm both launch gates and current restrictions before arranging your shuttle; the map does not authorize stops or scouting through closed parkland.
notices.sourceName: Washington State Parks — Riverside wildfire recovery

notices.title: Whitewater: local knowledge required
notices.text: This is a whitewater trip, not a casual float. State Parks advises whitewater experience and local knowledge. Published classifications vary with conditions: the existing section description lists Class II–III+, while Avista warns of downstream Class IV rapids. Get current local advice; the dotted course is not a safe passage through a rapid.
notices.sourceName: Avista river recreation map; Washington State Parks boating guidance

putInAccess.operator: City of Spokane Parks and Recreation
putInAccess.sourceName: City of Spokane — Downriver Park river access; Spokane Conservation District access inventory
putInAccess.note: City Parks documents the public non-motorized river access; the Conservation District documents its city ownership and boating use. Avista supplies the Meenach Bridge Park area coordinate. The Water Trail partner reported reopening of the seasonal gate in May 2025 following repair work; that report does not guarantee present gate status. Imagery corroborates the parking/facility vicinity. No exact landing, driving connector or verified bank is claimed.
putInAccess.directions: Use the signed river-access parking off Downriver Drive downstream of T.J. Meenach Bridge. This marker identifies the facility area beside the improved parking, not a shoreline ramp. Confirm seasonal gate and repair status with City Parks before arranging a shuttle.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Washington State Parks — Riverside State Park and October 28, 2026 reopening map
takeOutAccess.note: State Parks explicitly documents Plese Flats water access and its October 28, 2026 recovery map marks this facility open. Nearby fire-damaged trails remain closed. Coordinate provenance is separate: the approximate marker uses an OSM slipway checked against the visible bank approach and park facility, not an agency shoreline survey. Avista’s older area coordinate lies about 200 metres upstream/inland and is retained as research rather than substituted for the landing vicinity. No bank side or walking connector is verified.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the signed Plese Flats day-use access off Aubrey L. White Parkway, south of Seven Mile Road. Discover Pass required. State Parks lists the seasonal opening as April 1 until the first snow. This is a non-motorized access; check the gate and current park restrictions before the trip.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.
